record.paper_title: Open Problems in Affine Differential Geometry and Related Topics
record.original_question: A family of probability distributions {p(x, ξ)} determines a statistical manifold. Conversely, if a statistical manifold is given abstractly, what conditions are necessary and sufficient for there to exist a family of probability distributions whose induced statistical manifold structure coincides with the given one? What is the corresponding criterion in the special case of dually flat manifolds?

evidence.quote: The space spanned by probability distributions {p(x, ξ)} becomes a statistical manifold (cf. [2] and [13]). Conversely, if a statistical manifold is given, what is the condition that there exists the corresponding probability distributions which coincides the given statistical manifold? How about the dually flat manifolds case?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A statistical manifold is a smooth manifold $M$ equipped with a Riemannian metric $g$ and a totally symmetric $(0,3)$-tensor $C$ (the cubic, or Amari–Chentsov, tensor). Such a structure determines a one-parameter family of torsion-free affine connections $\nabla^{(\alpha)}$ on $M$ via $g(\nabla^{(\alpha)}_X Y, Z) = g(\nabla^{LC}_X Y, Z) - \tfrac{\alpha}{2}\, C(X,Y,Z)$, where $\nabla^{LC}$ is the Levi-Civita connection of $g$. The structure $(M,g,C)$ is called dually flat if there exists $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$ such that both $\nabla^{(\alpha)}$ and its $g$-dual $\nabla^{(-\alpha)}$ are flat affine connections.

Conversely, given a measure space $(\Omega,\mu)$ and a smooth family of probability densities $\{p(x;\xi)\}_{\xi\in M}$ on $\Omega$ parametrized by $M$, one obtains a statistical manifold structure on $M$ via the Fisher information metric
$$g_{ij}(\xi) = \int_{\Omega} \partial_i \log p(x;\xi)\,\partial_j \log p(x;\xi)\,p(x;\xi)\,d\mu(x),$$
and the cubic tensor
$$C_{ijk}(\xi) = \int_{\Omega} \partial_i \log p(x;\xi)\,\partial_j \log p(x;\xi)\,\partial_k \log p(x;\xi)\,p(x;\xi)\,d\mu(x).$$

Problem.
(a) Find necessary and sufficient conditions on an abstract statistical manifold $(M,g,C)$ ensuring the existence of a measure space $(\Omega,\mu)$ and a smooth parametric family of probability densities $\{p(x;\xi)\}_{\xi\in M}$ on $\Omega$ whose induced Fisher metric and cubic tensor coincide with $g$ and $C$.

(b) Specialize to the dually flat case: characterize those dually flat statistical manifolds $(M,g,C)$ which are realized in this way by a parametric family of probability distributions, and identify when the realizing family can be taken to be an exponential family (or a mixture family).
artifact.status_search_result: The realization problem for abstract statistical manifolds was largely settled by H. V. Lê, who proved that every smooth statistical manifold can be embedded into the space of probability measures on some (possibly finite) set, giving a positive answer to the original question of Amari and Lauritzen. In the dually flat case, it is classical that any (regular) dually flat structure is locally induced by an exponential family via a Bregman/Legendre construction. Refinements concerning global realizations, regularity, and minimal sample-space dimension continue to be studied, so the problem is best described as partially solved rather than completely closed.

status_evidence.title: Statistical manifolds are statistical models
status_evidence.snippet: Any smooth statistical manifold can be embedded into the space of probability measures on a finite set, giving a positive answer to an open problem of Amari and Lauritzen.
status_evidence.claim: Lê's theorem realizes any smooth statistical manifold as a statistical model, partially resolving the realization problem.

status_evidence.title: Information Geometry and Its Applications: Convex Function and Dually Flat Manifold
status_evidence.snippet: A dually flat manifold can be constructed beginning with a convex function; exponential families are universal representations of dually flat statistical manifolds.
status_evidence.claim: In the dually flat case, the structure is realized (locally) by an exponential family via a convex potential.

status_evidence.title: Information geometry - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Any dually flat statistical manifold, given by a regular Bregman divergence, uniquely induces a regular exponential family.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms the dually flat case is essentially answered through Bregman/Legendre duality and exponential families.
